parsed.narrative: With the default choices, modelled on the original paper, a hurricane with a feminine name is predicted to cause +4.1 additional deaths (95% CI -3.0 to 11.2), p = 0.257, n = 92 storms, so the verdict is NO CLEAR EVIDENCE. The minimal flip changes Choose which storms to analyse from "Drop the two deadliest storms" to "Keep every storm". 3 of the 14 single-decision changes reach FEMININE NAMES DEADLIER: keep every storm; drop only the deadliest storm; damage in 2013 dollars. That flip was re-executed from a fresh sandbox and reproduced exactly. The published specification curve over 1,728 specifications finds only 37 significant effects in the predicted direction (2.1%), with a median of 1.56 additional deaths, so the finding lives in a small corner of the analysis space.
caveats: The effect is a difference in predicted deaths at sample means, not a causal estimate for any one storm.
Ninety-four storms is a small sample and two of them dominate the death counts.
Scripted run: the plan was written by hand from the published specification menu, not proposed by a model.
